accepted.sentence: In Uganda, cooking varieties are steamed and mashed into matoke, a filling staple often served with savory sauces.
Thin slices of unripe fruit are fried into crisp chips, a popular snack in several tropical countries.
Because it contains no gluten, flour made from green fruit can help diversify baking options for people avoiding wheat.
In some communities, broad leaves serve as disposable plates for presenting cooked foods, reducing reliance on manufactured tableware.
Ripe pulp can be fermented into vinegar, providing a tart condiment for cooking and seasoning.
Chopped harvest residues can be fed into anaerobic digesters, where microbes produce biogas for usable energy.
On tropical slopes, dense roots can help hold soil in place and reduce erosion around cultivated fields.
In some regions, cooked green pieces provide a filling alternative to potatoes in savory meals.
